architecture: v2 (round 2 redesign of the decisive step)
slot_note: Forecasting block, second build of the wave; seed FC04 (station maturity ramp) not used: its forward-maturity driver repeats the age-forward structure of task132 drawn the same day, so the slot keeps the objective and draws a fresh world
niche: a non-bank consumer lender's quarter-end expected credit loss allowance on its unsecured personal loan book, with each product's default and repayment experience by month on book read from the loan system's record, which took over the earlier platform's open loans when the system went live in October 2019
answer: Book a collective expected credit loss allowance of AUD 13.2 million on the PL36 and PL60 personal loans at 30 September 2026.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who stages the book cleanly, reads CRM-ECL-04 and the record's dictionary entry correctly and builds the textbook PD from monthly default and repayment rates by month on book over every loan in the record, counting each from its drawdown, books AUD 11.6 million against AUD 13.2 million (12.3 per cent low), because the loans taken over at the October 2019 go-live are survivors whose months before it could not end in a recorded default or closing.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each loan's AASB 9 12-month or lifetime expected credit loss, whose PD term is the product's default probability by month on book estimated from a loan-level performance record with early repayment as a competing exit; with another field's nouns the staging triggers, the 2.4 scalar, LGD, re-amortised EAD and the scenario weights have nothing to attach to, so the task does not read the same.
layer1: a loan book extract with drawdown and first-repayment dates rather than months on book, repayment dates moved to the next NSW business day
a loan record that carries the earlier platform's loans under a lower numbering block from the October 2019 go-live, with default months at month ends and closures by reason

a hardship register joined by loan number, with arrangements that start, end and are cancelled, a status label as at the extract date moved by a Tuesday-night batch, and bulk-loaded COVID-19 deferrals whose status was never moved on
behaviour scores at origination and now on different scorecard versions with a published conversion

a prior quarter-end extract without the score column the job added in July, taken before the same change by a job that counted days past due to its morning run, beside month-end scoring runs dated the day after each month end
scenario multipliers and weights in a committee-approved workbook with the prior quarter's on a second sheet

a collections receipts ledger across cohorts with dishonour reversals, a debt-sale receipt carried without a loan number beside the sale schedule in cents per dollar of face value, and agency remittances posted by the reference they quote
a collection agency's placement report with its own column names and day-first dates, whose references the agency reissues after a placement closes
a collections MI file whose case resolution is set when the case closes, so a cure recorded on an approved arrangement stands after the arrangement is withdrawn
stakeholder_role: head of credit risk reporting at a consumer lender, who presents the quarter-end ECL allowance to the Audit and Risk Committee

spine.entity: one PL36 or PL60 loan the loan system has held since its October 2019 go-live, open or closed

world.org_type: non-bank consumer lender with an unsecured personal loan book

driver: A unit-level record that took over an earlier record's units holds them only if they were still present at the takeover, so the months they spent before it are months the record never watched, not months they were seen to come through; outcome rates by age must count each taken-over unit only from its age at the takeover, and counting it from its own start fills every early age's denominator with exposure that could not end in the outcome, so the rates and the forward total for a young population come out low.
driver_concrete: Bellbird's loan record holds the PL36 and PL60 loans drawn on the earlier platform from 2014 only if they were open when the loan system went live on 1 October 2019, so each product's default and repayment rates by month on book count a transferred loan only from its month on book at the go-live; counting it from drawdown adds its earlier months to every early month's loans at risk with no default possible and books the allowance about a tenth low.
stump: A strong solver builds each product's monthly default and repayment rates by month on book from the loan record, counting every loan from its drawdown, rolls each performing loan forward from its own month on book, and books AUD 11.6 million against AUD 13.2 million (12.3 per cent low); the step that lands it there is counting the 16,479 loans the record took over at the October 2019 go-live as at risk from their drawdown, when the record holds them only because they were still open that day.

differentiation.task132: task132 forecasts failures of replaceable modules in which a failed unit is renewed by a new one at age zero, so the forecast weights each band by the present module's survival and adds its replacement; here a loan defaults once and is not replaced, and the construction is the conditional increment of a filed curve for loans that have already survived part of it.
differentiation.task130: task130 runs a closed group off a rationed list; here nothing is rationed and no group closes: each loan's forward loss is a survival-conditioned share of a filed curve.
differentiation.task133: Round 2 moves the decisive step off the curve-conditioning chain v1 and v1 loop 1 used: there is no filed curve, the conditioning on survival and on both exits is the default path's own reflex (monthly default and repayment rates by month on book), and what decides is where a taken-over loan's exposure starts.
differentiation.task134: task134 v1 estimated a fixed-horizon probability from follow-up censored at the cut with competing exits, and its default construction landed; here the censoring and competing exits are the default path, and the decisive move is left truncation: loans the record took over count only from their month on book at the takeover.
differentiation.task180: task180 restores small events a detector masked during noisy hours, so its record misses events that happened; here every default of a taken-over loan after the takeover is recorded, and what the record lacks is the taken-over loans' months before it, so the move is where each loan's exposure starts (delayed entry), not a detection correction.

lineage.fate: hardening loop 1: survival to date landed on the portal (one model stumped, the other filed AUD 13,773,000 and scored 100 per cent, banking every inheriting ask: stage by product, drawdown year, stage 3 count)
lineage.driver: A cumulative outcome curve is filed from each unit's entry, and every unit in scope has already survived part of it, so its forward probability is the curve's remaining increments divided by its own survival to date; reading the curve from entry for every unit overstates the total, and shifting it to the unit's age without the division understates it.
lineage.stump: A competent solver applies the cumulative PD curve to each loan's remaining months counted from the reporting date as if it were a term structure and books an allowance about 43 per cent high; the step that lands it there is reading a curve indexed by months on book as if every performing loan were new.

lineage.fate: round 2 (2026-10-14): never judged on the portal; the 10/10 audit found it compliant but weak: a rung added above the step the v1 portal winner solved, with the development sample's outcome column beside a 'share of every loan drawn' header signposting it
lineage.driver: A cumulative outcome curve is filed as shares of every unit that ever entered, so units that left by a competing exit stay in its base; a unit still in scope at its age has come through both the outcome and the competing exit, so its forward probability is the curve's increment divided by the share of entrants still present and outcome-free at that age, which only the unit-level development record gives; dividing by one less the curve to date leaves the exited units in the base and understates the total, and a hazard rolled forward with no competing exit overstates it.
lineage.stump: A competent solver reads the PD curve as cumulative default by months on book, divides each loan's forward increments by its survival to date, 1 - C(a), and books about AUD 11.74 million against AUD 13,160,000, 10.8 per cent low; the step that lands it there is taking the curve's shares as shares of loans still open when they are shares of every loan drawn, so the loans repaid in full by month a stay in the at-risk base.

notes: Forcing event: the 30 September 2026 quarter close. Gate G forecasting repeats task132 by design: both builds sit in the Forecasting block; the mechanisms differ (task132 replacement of failed modules in a spares forecast, task133 conditioning a lifetime curve on survival to date). Realism rebuild 2026-10-11 moved the allowance to AUD 13,667,000 with realistic default levels. Forum redrawn at ship from committee_or_panel to board_of_directors (the Audit and Risk Committee chair presents to the board) after guard.py heart blocked committee_or_panel against task129. Hardening loop 1 (2026-10-11): the curve became the development sample's crude default share over complete-term cohorts, the answer moved to AUD 13,160,000, the inheriting asks were replaced by two decoupled asks (realised LGD of the 2023-24 defaults by product and quarter; where the 30 June stage 1 and stage 2 loans stand at 30 September), and the opening move moved from number-first to calendar-first. The pre-round repair moved it to deliverable-first (the chair's two slides first, the workbook behind them) after the clone check read one build order across the lane. Stage 6b (2026-10-11): ask devices hardened against the loop 1 round's careful solver (a June extract counting days past due to its 07:30 run; Collections MI cures recorded on collections arrangements withdrawn before they started); PLPD-2026.06 released as a smoothed curve fitted under the allowance's own constraints; CRM-ECL-04 and the run-folder dictionary rewritten as working documents. No change to the draw, the driver, the stump or the answer. Ship after portal round 1 (2026-10-11): the prompt converted to prompt.txt, question-first plain text at 840 characters with every ask carried word for word; no change to the draw, driver, stump or answer. Round 2 (2026-10-14): the 10/10 audit found the loop 1 design compliant but weak (a rung added above the step the v1 portal winner solved, the development sample signposting it); the decisive step moved to where a taken-over loan's exposure starts. The pack drops the curve and the development sample for the loan record; PD is read from the record by month on book (CRM-ECL-04 3.2 files the estimand, no method); the allowance is reported in AUD million to one decimal, and the estimators that use every loan correctly (delayed entry, the taken-over loans left out, landmark rates, the first-repayment clock) all file AUD 13.2 million. Ask A gains a second silent device (Wirraway reissues the references of closed placements and the receipts loader posts a remittance to the reference's first placement; the agency's placement report resolves it by date), and the A1 withdrawn-arrangement cures are drawn at a natural rate. Strategy relabelled from stated_rule_hard_construction: the decisive move is left truncation, a risk set filled with months the record never observed. Round 2 keeps the slot's draw (2026-10-11: the world, forum, forcing event and organisation) and edits the mechanism fields in place, as the brief keeps the world when the decisive step can move inside it; the context artifact is now the loan record (register), the forcing event the 30 September quarter close. Strategy maturity_censoring for the left truncation (the record holds the taken-over loans only from the go-live, so their earlier months are unobserved, not survived); population_selection names the same risk-set error from the denominator side and is banned against task132.
